los.text: Describe the position, form and functional anatomy of the gall bladder and biliary tree; their relations in the abdomen and the significance of these relations to gall bladder inflammation and biliary stones
los.html:
Gallbladder
  • Pear-shaped sac under the right lobe of the liver (gallbladder fossa)
  • Fundus, body, neck (Hartmann's pouch, where stones lodge), cystic duct (spiral valves of Heister).
  • Stores and concentrates bile (~50 mL).
Surface markingFundus at the tip of the right 9th costal cartilage (where the midclavicular line meets the costal margin).
RelationStructureSignificance
AboveLiverInflammation spreads to the liver bed
Below / behindDuodenum (1st and 2nd parts), transverse colon (hepatic flexure)Cholecystoenteric fistula → gallstone ileus (stone impacts at the ileocaecal valve)
In frontAnterior abdominal wall, peritoneumMurphy's sign (somatic pain once the parietal peritoneum is inflamed)
Diaphragm (via liver)Phrenic nerveShoulder-tip pain
Biliary colicVisceral pain in the epigastrium/right upper quadrant (foregut, T6–9), often after fatty food.
Cystic artery
  • Usually from the right hepatic artery, in Calot's triangle (cystic duct, common hepatic duct, inferior border of liver)
  • Tied at cholecystectomy.

los.text: Describe the journey of bile from the liver to the gallbladder and from the gallbladder to the duodenum
los.html:
1Hepatocytes secrete bile into bile canaliculi.
2. Bile ductules(canals of Hering)Interlobular bile ducts in the portal triads.
3. Right and left hepatic ductsCommon hepatic duct.
4Sphincter of Oddi closed (fasting) → bile backs up the cystic duct into the gallbladder, which concentrates it.
5Food (fat) in the duodenum → CCK → gallbladder contracts and the sphincter of Oddi relaxes.
6Bile flows down the cystic duct → common bile duct (behind the 1st part of duodenum, in or behind the head of pancreas).
7Joins the main pancreatic duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla (of Vater) → major duodenal papilla in the 2nd part of the duodenum.

los.text: Identify the head, neck, body and tail of the pancreas
los.html:
PartPosition
HeadIn the C-shaped curve of the duodenum, right of the SMV; uncinate process hooks behind the SMV/SMA
NeckIn front of the SMV/portal vein junction (L1, transpyloric plane)
BodyCrosses the aorta and left kidney, behind the stomach
TailEnds in the splenic hilum (splenorenal ligament): only intraperitoneal part

los.text: Describe the relationships of the pancreas with other abdominal organs
los.html:
DirectionRelations
In frontStomach (separated by the lesser sac), transverse mesocolon
Behind
  • IVC
  • Aorta
  • SMA and SMV (behind the neck, in front of the uncinate)
  • Portal vein formation
  • Common bile duct (behind the head)
  • Left renal vein
  • Left kidney and suprarenal
  • Splenic vein runs along the back of the body
Right2nd part of duodenum
LeftSpleen
  • Retroperitoneal (except the tail).

los.text: Discuss the significance of these relationships with respect to pancreatitis and biliary stone disease
los.html:
RelationshipConsequence
CBD runs through/behind the head and shares the ampullaGallstones obstructing the ampulla → acute pancreatitis; head cancer → painless obstructive jaundice with a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier)
Behind the stomach, in the lesser sacInflammatory fluid collects there → pseudocyst; pain radiates to the back
On the coeliac plexus and aortaSevere epigastric pain through to the back; coeliac plexus block for cancer pain
Splenic vein along the backSplenic vein thrombosis → gastric varices
Neck over the SMV/portal veinTumour invasion decides whether it can be removed
RetroperitonealBleeding tracks to the flanks (Grey Turner's) and umbilicus (Cullen's)
Head next to the duodenumLarge tumours or annular pancreas → duodenal obstruction

los.text: Recognise the main duct of the pancreas running the full length of the organ, beginning in the tail and ending in the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla with the bile duct (hepato-pancreatic ampulla of Vater)
los.html:
Main pancreatic duct (of Wirsung)Begins in the tail, runs the full length, turns down in the head and joins the bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla (of Vater) → major duodenal papilla (2nd part of the duodenum, ~10 cm from the pylorus).
Sphincter of OddiControls outflow; ERCP passes through it.
Accessory duct (of Santorini)Drains the upper head via the minor papilla (about 2 cm above).

los.text: Recognise the arterial supply and venous and lymphatic drainage of the pancreas
los.html:
HeadNeck, body, tail
ArteriesSuperior pancreaticoduodenal (gastroduodenal → coeliac) and inferior pancreaticoduodenal (SMA): a coeliac–SMA anastomosisSplenic artery branches (dorsal and great pancreatic)
VeinsPancreaticoduodenal veins → SMV and portal veinSplenic vein → portal vein
LymphPancreaticoduodenal nodes → superior mesenteric and coeliac nodesPancreaticosplenic nodes → coeliac nodes
  • Foregut/midgut boundary: the head sits where coeliac and SMA territories meet, so it has a double supply.
  • Endocrine output (insulin, glucagon) drains into the portal system, reaching the liver first.

los.text: Recognise the anatomy of the gall bladder and biliary tree on radiographic images and recognise biliary stones
los.html:
TestShowsUse
UltrasoundGallstones (bright with an acoustic shadow), wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, dilated ductsFirst-line for biliary disease
Plain X-rayOnly ~10–15% of gallstones are radio-opaque; porcelain gallbladder; air in the biliary treeNot used to find stones
MRCPBile and pancreatic ducts without contrast or instrumentsDuct stones, strictures (diagnostic)
ERCPDucts filled with contrast via an endoscopeTreats CBD stones (sphincterotomy, stone removal, stent); risk of pancreatitis
CTPancreatitis complications, tumoursStaging
  • Normal CBD: up to ~6 mm (larger after cholecystectomy and with age)
    • dilated ducts above a block suggest a stone or tumour.
